Gym Workout Checklist

A productive gym session isn't about doing more — it's about warming up properly, working each muscle group with good form, and leaving enough in the tank to cool down. This checklist walks through a balanced full-body session from your first warm-up set to logging your last lift. It's general fitness guidance, not personal training advice — adjust the exercises and weights to your level, and see the rest of our health and fitness checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Gym Workout Checklist · 15 items

  1. 1
    Set today's focus — full body, or a specific split like push, pull, or legs

    Knowing the target keeps you from wandering randomly between machines.

  2. 2
    Warm up for 5 to 10 minutes with light cardio to raise your heart rate
  3. 3
    Do dynamic mobility drills for the joints you're about to train

    Leg swings, arm circles, and bodyweight squats prime the muscles better than static stretching.

  4. 4
    Start with the biggest compound lifts while you're fresh — squats, deadlifts, bench, or rows

    Heavy, technical lifts belong early, before fatigue hurts your form.

  5. 5
    Work your upper body with a push and a pull movement
  6. 6
    Work your lower body with a squat or hinge and a single-leg movement
  7. 7
    Finish the main work with focused core exercises
  8. 8
    Use a weight you can control with good form for every rep

    If your form breaks down, the weight is too heavy — drop it.

  9. 9
    Rest 60 to 120 seconds between heavy sets, less for lighter accessory work
  10. 10
    Track each exercise, weight, and reps as you go

    Logging is how you know to add weight next time — progressive overload drives results.

  11. 11
    Sip water throughout the session, not just at the end
  12. 12
    Wipe down each machine and bench, and rerack your weights

    Basic gym etiquette — leave equipment as you'd want to find it.

  13. 13
    Cool down with 5 minutes of easy movement to bring your heart rate down
  14. 14
    Stretch the muscles you trained while they're still warm
  15. 15
    Log the session and note how it felt for next time

Frequently asked questions

How long should a gym workout be? expand_more

Most effective sessions run 45 to 75 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down. Beyond that, focus and form usually fade and the extra time adds little. Quality and consistency beat marathon sessions — a focused hour a few times a week does far more than an occasional two-hour grind.

Should I do cardio or weights first? expand_more

Do whichever matches your main goal first, while you're fresh. If strength or muscle is the priority, lift first and save cardio for the end or a separate day. If endurance is the goal, run first. A short easy cardio warm-up before lifting is fine either way — that's different from a hard cardio session.

In what order should I do gym exercises? expand_more

Warm up first, then do your biggest compound lifts — squats, deadlifts, presses, rows — while you have the most energy and focus. Move to smaller isolation and accessory work after, and finish with core and a cool-down. Training the heaviest, most technical movements early protects your form and lowers injury risk.
